entries.title: atoi
entries.summary: Convert a string to an int (no error detection).
entries.description: Skips leading whitespace and reads an optional sign and digits; stops at the first other character. Returns 0 when there is no number, so you cannot tell "0" from "abc". Use `strtol` when errors matter.

entries.title: atof
entries.summary: Convert a string to a double.
entries.description: Like `atoi` for floating point; no error detection. Use `strtod` for that.

entries.title: strtol
entries.summary: Convert a string to a long, with error detection and a base.
entries.syntax: long strtol(const char *s, char **end, int base);
entries.description: Sets `*end` to the first character not converted: when `*end == '\0'` the whole string was a number; `*end == s` means no digits at all. Overflow sets `errno` to `ERANGE`. `base` 10 for decimal, 16 for hexadecimal, 0 to detect `0x` and `0`.

entries.title: strtod
entries.summary: Convert a string to a double, with error detection.
entries.description: Works like `strtol`: `*end` points after the converted text.

entries.title: abs
entries.description: `abs(INT_MIN)` overflows. Use `labs` for long and `fabs` for double.

entries.title: rand
entries.description: The sequence is the same every run unless you seed it once with `srand`. For a number in [0, n) use `rand() % n` (slightly biased but fine for exercises).

entries.title: srand
entries.description: Call it once at the start. The same seed gives the same sequence, which is useful to reproduce a run.

entries.title: qsort
entries.syntax: void qsort(void *base, size_t n, size_t size, int (*cmp)(const void *, const void *));
entries.description: Sorts `n` elements of `size` bytes in place. `cmp` receives pointers to two ELEMENTS and returns negative, 0 or positive. For ints compare with `(x > y) - (x < y)` (subtracting can overflow); for an array of `char *` the callback receives `char **`.
mistakes: Treating the callback arguments as elements instead of pointers to them.

entries.title: bsearch
entries.summary: Binary search in a sorted array.
entries.syntax: void *bsearch(const void *key, const void *base, size_t n, size_t size, int (*cmp)(const void *, const void *));
entries.description: The array must be sorted with the same ordering as `cmp`. Returns a pointer to a matching element or NULL.
entries.example: int *p = bsearch(&key, v, n, sizeof v[0], cmp_int);

entries.title: system
entries.description: Starts a shell to run `command` and waits for it. Returns the command's status (use `WEXITSTATUS`). Never build the command from untrusted text.
mistakes: Passing user input to the shell.

entries.title: time
entries.description: `time(NULL)` returns the current calendar time. Often used as a seed: `srand(time(NULL))`.

entries.title: clock
entries.summary: Processor time used by the program.
entries.description: Divide the difference of two calls by `CLOCKS_PER_SEC` to get seconds of CPU time.
